subject: pi
title: Sessions are entry trees: /fork /clone /tree navigation with branch-switch summarization
one_why: Returning to an earlier point never destroys the abandoned path, and the abandoned path is summarized into the new branch instead of being lost - checkpoint-revert without losing either outcome.

subject: pi
title: Threshold compaction over a projected-context estimator rather than raw token counts
one_why: shouldCompact measures estimateProjectedContextTokens (what the model would actually receive incl. tools/system), so triggers don't drift from billed reality.

subject: pi
title: Prompt cache accounting plus an active cache-warmer in core
one_why: Measures hit economics and pre-warms the stable prefix so the first turn after idle isn't a full-price miss; no other anchor treats cache as an active feature.

subject: pi
title: Project-trust store gates loading of project settings, packages, and extensions before first prompt
one_why: Extension code is treated as project-executable content with an explicit per-cwd trust decision incl. session-only option - the cheapest defense against repo-supplied extension RCE.

subject: pi
title: Permission gates, destructive-confirm, repo guards shipped as example extensions over a blocking beforeToolCall
one_why: Core guarantees only that a hook can block a tool with a reason returned to the model; policy is user-composable rather than hardcoded - the inverse of cline's built-in guard (cline-4).

subject: pi
title: No built-in approvals or sandbox: bare pi executes arbitrary bash as the user
evidence: SECURITY.md:50 ("intentionally does not have a sandbox"), packages/coding-agent/src/core/bash-executor.ts
one_why: Documented honestly with containerization recipes, but out-of-the-box a prompt-injected command has full user privileges; acceptable only for users who follow the docs.

subject: pi
title: Security doc states exactly what the harness does not protect against, with three containerization patterns
one_why: A template for honest threat-modeling copy: scope of protection, what is out of scope, and concrete containment recipes - directly quotable for hotdog.

subject: pi
title: Loop tested by a scripted generation harness driving stream events
one_why: Nuance vs codex-5/cline-2: harness drives the loop's stream-fn abstraction rather than mocking an HTTP wire format - cheaper but tests less of the transport layer.

subject: pi
title: RPC and JSON app modes with a documented command protocol and client/server packages
one_why: Headless operation is a first-class mode of the same engine (not a bolted-on exec flag), enabling IDE/automation embedding without forking the loop.
